findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/evidence/environment-contract.ts:544 — HIGH: producer trust is self-asserted by the receipt: normalization accepts verificationSource=verifier-owned-attestation-registry plus signatureVerified=true without resolving a verifier-owned registry, signature, or key binding; evaluateEvidenceEnvironmentGateProjection then hard-codes environmentDescriptorValid/environmentReceiptValid/environmentPolicyValid to true. A caller can therefore mint two invented lineage/key/session tuples, normalize both, and satisfy evaluateEvidenceEnvironmentQuorum. WHY: this contradicts the identity-bound, forged-producer fail-closed invariant and makes host-independence evidence forgeable.
findings.resolvedReason: Repro: prior receipt fields could self-assert signatureVerified and invented producer tuples. Root cause: trust identity lived inside the untrusted receipt and Gate accepted a pre-normalized envelope. Fix: receipt now carries only an opaque producerAttestationRef; verifier-owned resolver returns verified identity outside the receipt, and Gate re-normalizes raw inputs. Repro test: evidence-environment smoke rejects unresolved attestations and forged quorum; PASS at b31b29b522.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/evidence/environment-contract.ts:793 — HIGH: M5 is described as actual lifecycle Gate integration, but evaluateEvidenceEnvironmentGateProjection is referenced only by the smoke test and no REVIEW/TEST/DONE state-machine consumer invokes it. The new process-fact entry merely names a consumer; it does not make the receipt gate-consumed. WHY: the public support matrix currently upgrades a pure library projection to an implemented lifecycle-control claim, leaving the Story/Release combination gap unchanged.
findings.resolvedReason: Repro: reference search previously found the projection only in the smoke helper. Root cause: no production lifecycle consumer. Fix: evaluateDoneRequiredEvidence now calls validateDoneRequiredEvidenceEnvironmentProjection, which projects every canonical DONE_REQUIRED receipt and invokes evaluateEvidenceEnvironmentGateProjection. Repro test: done-required-validation-smoke exercises this production evaluator; PASS at b31b29b522.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-evidence-environment-adapter-execution-plan.md:62,936-942 claims the EEA mechanism is integrated/demonstrated at a lifecycle Gate, but repository call-site search shows evaluateEvidenceEnvironmentGateProjection is referenced only by exports, process-fact declarations, and packages/main/src/tasks/evidence-environment-adapter-smoke.ts; no TEST/DONE/storyMachine or other production lifecycle Gate consumes normalized EEA receipts. The smoke directly calls the helper with fabricated checks, so it proves the helper projection, not M5 actual Gate integration. WHY: the paper must remain at Level B and CHK-006/M5 is incomplete until a real configured lifecycle Gate consumer invokes the projection and a test exercises that consumer end-to-end.
findings.resolvedReason: Repro: documentation claimed lifecycle integration while only smoke code called the helper. Root cause: support matrix outpaced implementation. Fix: actual DONE_REQUIRED call chain is implemented and documented as evaluateDoneRequiredEvidence -> validateDoneRequiredEvidenceEnvironmentProjection -> Gate projection. Repro test: done-required lifecycle smoke and process-fact contract PASS at b31b29b522.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-evidence-environment-adapter-execution-plan.md:907-910 requires an exact manuscript artifact path/version plus implementation commit or release digest before M6 is complete, but the repository only names the existing arXiv identifier in README and does not bind a manuscript revision/artifact to the B-955c implementation commit/release; CHK-005 is nevertheless marked done. WHY: the handoff cannot yet satisfy its own audit rule, and an external editor cannot tell which manuscript version contains the calibrated EEA claim. Record the exact manuscript target/version and binding digest, or explicitly leave M6/CHK-005 incomplete and state that current claims are repository-document-only.
findings.resolvedReason: Repro: no external manuscript revision/path plus implementation digest exists. Root cause: M6 language conflated the repository paper-facing artifact with an external manuscript handoff. Fix: document now names the exact repository artifact, explicitly marks external M6 incomplete, states no external manuscript path/revision/release digest is bound, and limits the external manuscript claim to Level B. CHK-005 covers the repository paper-facing abstraction only; no external Level C claim remains. Documentation audit at b31b29b522 confirms the honest downgrade.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/evidence/environment-contract.ts:793-819 [high] Gate projection trusts caller-supplied NormalizedEvidenceEnvironmentEnvelope and overwrites environmentDescriptorValid/environmentReceiptValid/environmentPolicyValid to true; it only checks that semanticDigest is non-empty and never rechecks semantic/policy digest, subject binding, or freshnessDeadline at consumption time. Repro against built dist: a JSON-cloned envelope with forged subject/output/digests and an expired freshnessDeadline still returns {decision:"advance",allowed:true,reasons:[]}; an honestly normalized envelope also continues to advance after its deadline because the API has no current-time/freshness verification. WHY: this violates CHK-006 forged/stale fail-closed and lets untrusted/stale evidence gain lifecycle Gate force. Require a verifier-owned envelope validation/re-normalization or signed opaque provenance plus consumption-time freshness/digest checks; add direct Gate-level forged and post-normalization expiry regressions.
findings.resolvedReason: Repro: cloned normalized envelope could be altered or expire and still advance. Root cause: Gate trusted caller-normalized data and did not perform consumption-time validation. Fix: Gate accepts only raw descriptor id, invocation, and receipt; resolves the private default registry, verifies invocation/receipt digests and bindings, and rechecks freshness at Gate time. Direct forged subject, forged receipt, and post-normalization expiry regressions PASS at b31b29b522.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/evidence/environment-contract.ts:549-563,833-858 [high] Producer attestation is not verifier-owned in implementation: normalize accepts producerId/lineageId/keyId/sessionId, verificationSource, trustClass, and signatureVerified directly from the caller receipt, and quorum trusts those booleans/strings. A caller can submit two invented attestations with signatureVerified:true and distinct arbitrary IDs; both normalize and evaluateEvidenceEnvironmentQuorum returns independent:true (the existing smoke itself does exactly this for codex-host/claude-host). WHY: the string literal verificationSource does not prove registry verification, so forged producers can manufacture independent quorum, contradicting CHK-006 and the documented authority separation. Resolve attestations through a verifier-owned registry/verification callback or accept only an opaque verified-attestation handle; also make quorum enforce its required cardinality/policy rather than treating empty or one-element input as independent.
findings.resolvedReason: Repro: two caller-invented signatureVerified attestations could satisfy quorum, including empty/one-element ambiguity. Root cause: self-attested trust and absent cardinality floor. Fix: opaque refs resolve through verifier-owned resolver; quorum re-normalizes raw items and requires at least two verified producers with distinct lineage, key, and session. Zero, one, duplicate, and unresolved cases fail; smoke PASS at b31b29b522.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/evidence/environment-contract.ts:488-565,793-819 — HIGH: normalization accepts any structurally valid caller-supplied descriptor without resolving it through the default registry, and Gate projection then hard-codes environmentDescriptorValid/environmentReceiptValid/environmentPolicyValid=true. Repro against the built artifact created descriptor id `unregistered.evil`; normalization returned ok=true and DONE_REQUIRED projection returned decision=advance with no reasons. This violates the registered-descriptor fail-closed invariant and is not covered by the smoke suite.
findings.resolvedReason: Repro: caller-supplied descriptor unregistered.evil could normalize and advance. Root cause: normalization accepted arbitrary descriptor objects and Gate hard-coded descriptor validity. Fix: Gate resolves only the default registered descriptor by id and requires exact canonical descriptor equality during normalization. Unregistered descriptor Gate regression returns stop; PASS at b31b29b522.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/evidence/environment-contract.ts:793 and packages/main/src/core/process-fact-levels.ts:395 — HIGH: the claimed L4 lifecycle Gate integration is only a standalone exported helper exercised by `evidence-environment-adapter-smoke.ts`; repository reference search finds no story machine, phase gate, DONE-required handler, or other existing lifecycle consumer calling it. The self-test can pass while real Task/Story/Release gates never consume an EEA receipt, so CHK-006 happy-path integration evidence is missing.
findings.resolvedReason: Repro: process-fact L4 declaration named a consumer that did not exist. Root cause: registry prose was not backed by a production call site. Fix: DONE_REQUIRED evidence evaluator now invokes the EEA Gate for every receipt; process-fact owner and consumer point to the real call chain. Production evaluator tampered environment/executable identity regressions and process-fact verifier PASS at b31b29b522.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/evidence-environment-adapter-smoke.ts:141-193 — MEDIUM: the plan explicitly requires error/timeout handling, and the contract defines fail/error/timeout/cancelled/unavailable statuses, but the smoke never constructs any non-pass status (the only `timeout` occurrences are timeoutMs configuration). Add normalization/Gate cases for fail, error, timeout, cancelled, and unavailable with stable reason expectations so status semantics cannot regress silently.
findings.resolvedReason: Repro: smoke covered only pass status despite five non-pass contract statuses. Root cause: missing status matrix. Fix: Gate-level fail, error, timeout, cancelled, and unavailable cases now assert deterministic stop reason codes receipt_failed, checker_error, receipt_timeout, receipt_cancelled, receipt_unavailable. Evidence-environment smoke PASS at b31b29b522.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/evidence/environment-contract.ts:916 — HIGH: F-001 remains unresolved at the resolver trust boundary. The receipt now carries only an opaque ref, but evaluateEvidenceEnvironmentQuorum accepts an arbitrary caller-supplied EvidenceEnvironmentAttestationResolver, and the only implementation is the smoke test local Map at packages/main/src/tasks/evidence-environment-adapter-smoke.ts:218. A caller can return two invented VerifiedEvidenceEnvironmentProducerIdentity rows and satisfy independence; there is no project-owned pinned-producer registry, Ed25519/public-key/session binding, or revocation check required by the candidate spec at lines 737-753. WHY: moving self-asserted identity from the receipt into an untrusted callback does not make it verifier-owned, so forged distinct-Host quorum is still mechanically possible despite the support claim.
findings.resolvedReason: Repro: b31b29b522 accepted an arbitrary caller EvidenceEnvironmentAttestationResolver, so callback-minted identities could satisfy quorum. Root cause: an injected callback was treated as a verifier-owned trust root without pinned keys, signed session/invocation/subject binding, or revocation. Fix: removed the resolver and verified-identity types from the public/runtime contract; opaque refs never upgrade trust, and distinct-host quorum is explicitly fail-closed unsupported with distinct_host_quorum_unsupported until a project-owned cryptographic registry exists. Regression: a callback-shaped extra property returning invented identities cannot advance quorum; EEA smoke PASS at c0c3eeddde.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/evidence/environment-contract.ts:924-966 [high] F-006 remains bypassable: quorum deduplicates lineageId/keyId/sessionId but never producerId. Repro against commit b31b29b522 build: two resolver-verified identities with the same producerId="same-host" and distinct lineage/key/session values produce {independent:true,reasons:[]}. WHY: CHK-006 explicitly requires same-producer inputs to fail closed; a producer able to rotate or mint lineage/key/session identifiers can still count twice. Track producerId in the independence set (and add the exact same-producer/distinct-other-identities regression), or define and mechanically enforce a stronger canonical producer principal supplied by the trusted resolver.
findings.resolvedReason: Repro: prior quorum omitted producerId deduplication, allowing same producerId with distinct lineage/key/session values. Root cause: incomplete independence dimensions combined with an untrusted resolver. Fix: selected the safe unsupported branch: no producer identity tuple is accepted at all without a pinned registry; every distinct-host quorum is independent=false, repeated opaque principal references additionally return same_producer_not_independent. Regression injects the same producerId with distinct lineage/key/session callback rows and still receives distinct_host_quorum_unsupported; repeated principal regression also fails; EEA smoke PASS at c0c3eeddde.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/done-required-validation.ts:690-695 and 587-617 — HIGH: runDoneRequiredValidation explicitly omits effectiveEnvironmentDigest/executableDigest on process.platform === win32, while evaluateDoneRequiredEvidence unconditionally calls validateDoneRequiredExecutionIdentityCoverage, which rejects every missing value. Therefore any Windows project with a configured DONE-required policy will produce its own evidence and then deterministically fail with effective-environment-digest-mismatch/executable-digest-mismatch; no Windows/platform-branch test covers this. Preserve fail-closed identity semantics with a Windows-capable producer/validator contract rather than emitting evidence that can never pass.
findings.resolvedReason: Repro: Windows producer omitted effectiveEnvironmentDigest/executableDigest while the consumer required them, making every configured DONE-required Gate fail. Root cause: execution used an implicit Windows shell but identity recorded only declared shell mode and producer skipped identity entirely. Fix: producer and consumer now share buildDoneRequiredExecutionIdentity; receipts always persist environment, target executable, and conditional shellExecutableDigest; validation-executor records actual Windows shell=true; win32 resolves and hashes ComSpec/cmd.exe separately from the target executable. Regression: platform-injected fake cmd.exe asserts producer/consumer digest equality and actual commandSpec shell=true; DONE-required and validation-evidence-reuse smokes PASS at c0c3eeddde.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-evidence-environment-adapter-execution-plan.md:901-902 still states as M5 acceptance that a distinct-Host policy accepts separately attested producers, while the support matrix (line 65), I1 (lines 241-244), README, architecture doc, and current evaluateEvidenceEnvironmentQuorum implementation explicitly reject every distinct-host quorum as distinct_host_quorum_unsupported until a pinned registry exists. WHY: this leaves the same normative document claiming both supported acceptance and fail-closed unsupported behavior, so reviewers can incorrectly count producer independence as implemented. Rewrite the M5 bullet to require unsupported/fail-closed now and separately state the future acceptance condition after the pinned-key/session/revocation registry exists.
findings.resolvedReason: Repro: M5 acceptance still said current distinct-Host policy accepts separately attested producers, contradicting the implemented unsupported Gate. Root cause: future cryptographic-registry acceptance language remained in the current milestone. Fix: M5 now requires current distinct-Host policy to return distinct_host_quorum_unsupported and states separately that only a future project-owned pinned-key, signed producer/session/invocation/subject and revocation-checked registry may enable acceptance. Docs drift and explicit stale-phrase scan PASS at 9576d35896.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/done-required-validation.ts:526-530,695-700 — HIGH: F-012 remains open end-to-end. On Windows runValidationCommand now correctly reports the actual implicit shell as result.shell=true, and the producer persists receipt.shell=true, but validateRequiredReceiptCoverage still derives expectedShell only from the configured command.shell (normally false). Every ordinary structured Windows DONE-required command therefore fails with receipt-shell-mismatch before the new dual executable identity can pass. The added platform seam test only compares buildDoneRequiredExecutionIdentity outputs and constructs a CommandSpec; it never evaluates a Windows-shaped receipt through validateRequiredReceiptCoverage/evaluateDoneRequiredEvidence, so this regression is not detected. Make receipt coverage consume the same actual execution identity/platform seam and add an end-to-end Windows-shaped evaluator case preserving non-shell configuration intent while binding target executableDigest plus actual shellExecutableDigest.
findings.resolvedReason: Repro: validateRequiredReceiptCoverage compared receipt.shell to configured command.shell, so an ordinary Windows implicit shell=true receipt failed before identity validation. Root cause: the base coverage Gate did not consume the shared actual execution identity. Fix: evaluateDoneRequiredEvidence builds one current execution identity and passes it to both receipt coverage and identity coverage; expected shell comes from that identity. End-to-end Windows-shaped fixture keeps configured shell=false, binds fake node.exe target digest plus fake ComSpec cmd.exe shell digest, records actual shell=true, traverses the full evaluator including EEA projection, and PASSes. POSIX and validation-reuse suites PASS at 9576d35896.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-evidence-environment-adapter-execution-plan.md:448-467,517-540 defines the implemented Windows shell binding as shellIdentityDigest over shell executable, implementation/version, launch mode, and init-file policy, while current code exposes shellExecutableDigest and hashes only the resolved shell executable content; line 113 also still says both identity surfaces currently record declared rather than actual Windows shell mode, contradicting the new support matrix and lines 642-648. WHY: the paper contract overstates the epistemic content of the implemented Windows evidence and simultaneously calls the closed gap open. Align the normative schema/name and identity semantics with shellExecutableDigest, explicitly scope richer shell/version/launch/init identity as future work, and update the stale repository-audit row.
findings.resolvedReason: Repro: normative prose claimed shellIdentityDigest covered shell version/login/init posture while code implements shellExecutableDigest over resolved shell executable content only, and repository audit still called the Windows gap open. Root cause: proposal schema outran the calibrated implementation. Fix: schema/table/prose now use shellExecutableDigest exclusively, define its exact content-only scope, mark version/login/init/switch posture as future versioned work, and update the audit row to actual shell=true plus ComSpec binding. Docs drift and stale-term scan PASS at 9576d35896.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/evidence/environment-contract.ts:641-656 and packages/main/src/core/validation-evidence-reuse.ts:128-149 [high] Final integration breaks existing policy-authorized compound shell commands. resolveDoneRequiredPolicy intentionally parses a string containing shell metacharacters (for example `node -e "process.exit(0)" && node -e "process.exit(0)"`) as one shell:true command. buildRoutineValidationIdentity then tries to resolve the entire compound command as a target executable, yielding executableDigest:null while correctly hashing /bin/sh. projectDoneRequiredReceiptToEnvironment unconditionally requires a non-empty target executableDigest, so a PASS receipt from this supported policy throws command_spec_mismatch and the production DONE_REQUIRED Gate can never pass. Repro against 9576d35896 produced shell=true, a valid shellExecutableDigest, executableDigest:null, then `executor-owned effective environment and executable identities are required`. WHY: the EEA lifecycle integration must not make an existing valid DONE policy permanently uncompletable. Either reject compound-shell policies at configuration time with an explicit unsupported error, or define a shell-command identity that binds the exact command text/CommandSpec plus shell executable without pretending there is one target executable; add a full evaluator regression for the chosen contract.
findings.resolvedReason: Repro: a policy-authorized compound shell string produced shell=true, executableDigest=null and a valid /bin/sh shellExecutableDigest, but EEA projection unconditionally required target executable identity. Root cause: direct-execution identity requirements were incorrectly applied to shell scripts with no single target executable. Fix: EEA CommandSpec now has conditional identity: shell=false requires non-null target executableDigest and forbids shell digest; shell=true requires non-null actual shellExecutableDigest, permits target executableDigest=null only when unresolved, and still digest-binds full command/args/cwd/environment/timeout/policy. Full evaluateDoneRequiredEvidence regression PASSes the compound policy and a tampered shell digest fails with shell-executable-digest-mismatch[0]. Build, EEA, DONE-required, validation-reuse, docs-drift, Pack, Quantum and process-fact checks PASS at 16988f6a57.
